title: SDLC Analysis Dataset Sidecar
description: Envelope/provenance schema for one dataset's sidecar file, '<id>-<name>.meta.json'. Written by the domain extractor agent AFTER its '<id>-<name>.jsonl' records file is complete, so a killed run never leaves a 'complete' sidecar over a partial records file. The records themselves are NOT described here — they are raw provider records and carry no derived fields. Prose contract: docs/output-contract.md.

dataset.description: Lowercase dataset id. Closed set of the 24 datasets: a1-a7 version control, b1-b5 CI/CD, c1-c6 tickets, d1-d6 incidents.

records_file.description: Filename of the JSONL records file this sidecar describes, e.g. 'a2-commits.jsonl'. Must be the filename fixed for this dataset id in docs/output-contract.md section 2 — renaming breaks --resume, the run manifest, and the validator.

provider.description: The source this dataset was extracted from, resolved at runtime rather than hard-wired.

name.description: Provider identifier as the plugin names it, e.g. 'github', 'azure-devops', 'jira', 'pagerduty'. Null exactly when no provider was connected for this domain, in which case completeness is 'unavailable'.

detected_via.description: Which of the two detection surfaces found the provider — MCP tools present, or a CLI on PATH. Null exactly when name is null: an unconnected provider was detected via nothing.

window.description: The time window the extraction was asked for, and the bounds it resolved to.

requested.description: The window argument as the user gave it, e.g. '6m'.

from.description: Resolved start of the window, verbatim — original UTC offset preserved, never normalised to Z.

to.description: Resolved end of the window, verbatim — original UTC offset preserved, never normalised to Z.

scope.description: What the dataset was extracted from, in the provider's own identifiers.

identifiers.description: Provider-native repository / project / service identifiers covered by this dataset. Empty array when the provider was unavailable.

note.description: How the scope was determined, when that is not obvious from the identifiers alone.

completeness.description: Closed three-state enum, always present. 'complete' = pagination genuinely ran to exhaustion and truncation is empty. 'truncated' = extraction started and stopped short, with at least one truncation record. 'unavailable' = nothing was retrieved, so record_count is 0, the JSONL is empty, unavailable_reason is set, truncation is empty (nothing extracted cannot have been cut off), and gaps.md carries a line. There is no fourth state and no absent value.

record_count.description: Number of lines in the records file. This is deliberate provenance, not a derived field: the 'no derived fields' prohibition binds the records, and this count is the only thing that makes silent truncation detectable — the validator compares it against the actual line count. See docs/output-contract.md section 4.

truncation.description: Every cutoff that occurred while extracting this dataset. Empty array when nothing was cut off. A non-empty array can coexist with completeness 'truncated' and with nothing else: with 'complete' it is the silent data loss the contract exists to prevent, and with 'unavailable' it is incoherent, because a dataset that was never extracted cannot have been cut off. Both contradictions are rejected by the allOf branches below.

extracted_at.description: When this dataset finished extracting, verbatim — original UTC offset preserved, never normalised to Z.

unavailable_reason.description: Why nothing could be retrieved, in the provider's terms, e.g. 'no incident-management MCP server connected' or 'pipelines_build exposes no timeline action'. Required when completeness is 'unavailable'.

truncation_record.description: The explicit marker written whenever extraction stopped short of exhaustion. It is the plugin's only bound on volume — there is no cap, no sampling and no dedupe — so it must carry enough for --resume to continue from the cutoff.

reason.description: 'rate_limited' = provider throttled after one retry. 'provider_cap' = the provider caps what it returns with no paginated alternative. 'pagination_unsupported' = no skip/continuation exists, so the first page is all there is. 'context_budget' = the extracting agent ran out of room to carry more records to disk. 'provider_error' = any other failure while paging.

detail.description: One sentence in the provider's own terms, naming the unreachable count when the provider reported a total.

at.description: When the cutoff happened, verbatim — original UTC offset preserved.

last_record_id.description: Provider-native id of the last record written to the JSONL. Null when the cutoff happened before any record landed.

last_record_timestamp.description: That record's timestamp, verbatim. Null when the cutoff happened before any record landed.

remaining_estimate.description: Records known to remain, when the provider reports a total. Omit rather than guess.

cursor.description: How to continue from the cutoff. A truncation record that cannot be resumed from is a contract defect.

resumable.description: True when the provider offers a continuation surface. False only when it genuinely offers none — never as a shortcut for 'the cursor was not recorded'.

resume_from.description: Provider-native parameters needed to replay the next page — continuation token, page number, skip, since-timestamp, last issue key, whatever that provider consumes. Free-form because it is the provider's vocabulary, not the plugin's.

unreachable_reason.description: Why no continuation exists, e.g. 'Jira changelog is capped at its most recent entries and no paginated-changelog tool exists' or 'repo_branch list accepts top but exposes no skip or continuation'. Required when resumable is false.
